sources.cite: Python 3.12 documentation (Indonesian translation, 3.12.16), The Python Tutorial, 5.1.3-5.1.4 List Comprehensions and Nested List Comprehensions
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the translated page (the English page did not appear in a search; the fetch gave the Indonesian text with its own translation and one untranslated English sentence). A matrix is a list of lists ('a 3x4 matrix implemented as a list of 3 lists of length 4'); the initial expression of a comprehension 'can be an arbitrary expression, including another list comprehension', evaluated for each iteration. That is why [["free"] * 12 for _ in range(8)] builds eight inner lists.

sources.cite: Python 3.15 documentation, Common Sequence Operations, note on s * n (not opened for this round)
sources.note: To verify: the standard library reference notes that items in s * n 'are not copied; they are referenced multiple times', with the [[]] * 3 example and the list comprehension fix. That page did not appear in a search for this round. Every behavior in the case follows from that rule: multiplying a list of one inner list repeats references to the same inner list.
